What to do first

2 minutes

Stop Claude Code from reading outside the project it is working in

Fixes this finding

Your Supabase service_role key: Claude Code can read it without asking youWhat is the service_role key? The Supabase key meant only for servers (service_role): it bypasses all the security rules of your database. It should not be on your computer unless it is essential.

With it anyone can read, change or delete everything in your database, bypassing all its protections. Right now Claude Code can read it from any of your 2 projects, and it has a way to send it out without anyone approving.What is auto mode? A Claude Code mode in which it asks you much less: reads and edits inside the project are approved on their own, and most other actions are decided by another AI model. Since version 2.1.283 it is the mode Claude Code starts in unless you choose another.

If you do this, your score rises from 30 to 32.
Edit the file %USERPROFILE%/.claude/settings.json and merge this content into what it already has, without deleting anything. Show me the change before saving.

{
  "permissions": {
    "blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories": true
  }
}

Paste them into Claude Code. It will show you the change and ask before making it. Run RosmarOps again.

›I'd rather do it by hand
  1. Open the file ~/.claude/settings.json with Notepad.What is settings.json? Claude Code's settings file for your user. It decides what Claude Code can do without asking you.
  2. Add these lines inside what is already there, without deleting anything:
    {
  "permissions": {
    "blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories": true
  }
}
  3. Save it and run RosmarOps again.

After this, Claude Code can only read it while you work inside a. To remove the risk completely, take the credential off this computer and change it at the provider.What is a .env file? A file where a project keeps its keys and passwords so it can run. It usually stays out of git, but it is still on your disk, and any program that can read your files can read it.

Urgent
›Claude Code can change Cursor's configuration

If someone tricks Claude Code, it can leave a program installed in Cursor that runs the next time you open it, without leaving a trace.What is an agent's configuration? The file where an agent lists the extra tools it starts when it opens (MCP servers). Whoever can write to it can make the agent run a new program.

If you fix this: 30 → 34

How to fix it
  1. Press the button to copy the instructions.
  2. Paste them into Claude Code. It will show you the change and ask before making it.
  3. Run RosmarOps again.
Edit the file %USERPROFILE%/.claude/settings.json and merge this content into what it already has, without deleting anything. Show me the change before saving.

{
  "permissions": {
    "ask": [
      "Edit(//h/.cursor/mcp.json)"
    ]
  }
}
›I'd rather do it by hand
  1. Open the file ~/.claude/settings.json with Notepad.
  2. Add these lines inside what is already there, without deleting anything:
    {
  "permissions": {
    "ask": [
      "Edit(//h/.cursor/mcp.json)"
    ]
  }
}
  3. Save it and run RosmarOps again.
This reduces the risk but does not remove it: other ways remain. Your score does not change until the warning disappears.
Technical details

Where: /h/.cursor/mcp.json

Medium confidence: one step depends on auto mode's classifier, which is a model, not a person.

  • Depends on auto mode's classifier allowing the step. The classifier is a model, not a person, and RosmarOps cannot predict its decision.
  • Assumes auto mode is available to your account and model; if it is not, Claude Code starts in manual mode.
  • Assumes you use the default mode. A mode you pick in the app or the IDE is not stored where RosmarOps can read it.

How to read it: «another AI model decides» means no person approves the step; an AI model judges it, and it can be wrong or be tricked. «Factory setting» is what the agent does unless you change it.

What we don't know

We assume Claude Code works as its documentation says, with your user's permissions, and that nothing blocks it. What depends on auto mode is decided by another AI model, not a person, and we cannot know in advance what it will decide.

Give it to your AI
